Data Appreciation · Week 12 · Title

Project: a data job, start to finish

Use everything from the term again on one real job: collect, organise, calculate, chart, share safely and back up.

Next Generation Genius · Year 1 · Foundation

Data Appreciation · Week 12 · Goals

By the end of today

  • Carry out a complete data task on your own
  • Use files, formulas, sorting, a chart and safe sharing together
  • Explain your choices to a panel
Data Appreciation · Week 12 · Idea 1

Understand it

This project uses every earlier week again. Go back to your notes from weeks 2, 6 and 11 before you start.

Your project needs:

  • a folder with date-first file names (week 2) and a backup (week 3);
  • data entered consistently (week 4) — at least 15 rows, collected with a Google Form or by hand;
  • a formatted table (week 5) with formulas for totals and averages (week 6);
  • sorted or filtered to answer one question (week 7);
  • one chart with a title that states the finding (week 8);
  • no unnecessary personal data, and consent where people are involved (week 10);
  • shared as a PDF and as a Restricted link with your instructor as commenter (week 11).
Data Appreciation · Week 12 · Idea 2

Understand it

The panel will ask about YOUR choices: why that format, why that chart, how it is backed up. That is how they know the work is yours.

Panel

Data Appreciation · Week 12 · Practice

Now you do it

  1. Choose a job: a class survey, a club budget, or a reading log
  2. Collect at least 15 rows of data
  3. Build, chart, share and present it

Need a hand? Use the checklist above as your plan: tick each line as you finish it.

Done early? Add a second sheet that summarises the first with COUNTIF and AVERAGE, and a second chart.

Data Appreciation · Week 12 · Assessment

How you will be assessed

  • Your data job: share the folder or sheet (Restricted, instructor as commenter) and the PDF, and describe what you did at each step.
  • Name one thing that would have gone wrong without your backup or your consistent data, and how you avoided it.

Your work is marked against the rubric, and you may be asked to explain your choices. Show your own thinking.

Data Appreciation · Week 12 · Home

At home this week

  • Rehearse your two-minute explanation
  • Check your backup: can you open the file from the second place?

Read and explore

  • Google Forms — Make a survey for free; the answers arrive in a spreadsheet.
  • GCFGlobal — Google Sheets — Step-by-step spreadsheet lessons with practice files; work through the one named in class.
  • Google Sheets function list — Look up any formula used today — AVERAGE, MEDIAN, MODE, COUNTIF.
